text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your fever and altered mentation, have you experienced any recent head trauma or seizures, and do you have a stiff neck?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, are you experiencing any muscle rigidity, tremors, or excessive sweating? I also need to know if you have had any difficulty speaking, swallowing, or moving your limbs.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: These symptoms strongly suggest Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome given your haloperidol use. To confirm this, I need to check your muscle enzyme levels and white blood cell count. REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase, Complete Blood Count
